en.question: A payment-adjustment endpoint is backed by a Claude agent with a refund tool. Network timeouts cause the client to retry, and some customers receive two refunds. Which fix addresses the actual defect?

options.text: Instruct the agent in the system prompt never to issue a refund twice.
options.note: The duplicate originates in the network layer, which no prompt can reach.

options.text: Remove client retries so a timeout surfaces to the user as an error.
options.note: Removes a useful recovery path and still leaves the first refund ambiguous.

options.text: Log every refund and run a nightly reconciliation job to reverse duplicates.
options.note: Detects the damage after the customer has already been paid twice.

options.text: Require an idempotency key so a repeated call returns the original result.

en.explanation: The request may have succeeded before the timeout, so the retry is legitimate. Only an idempotency key lets the server recognise the repeat and decline to act twice.
